about: Links this machine to its Nerve centers.

options.line: Where node.toml and the keys live
options.more: Where node.toml and the keys live [env: NERVE_NODE_CONFIG_DIR] [default: ~/.config/nerve, or /etc/nerve when installed as a service]
options.name: --config-dir <CONFIG_DIR>

options.line: Where the control socket and the audit log live
options.more: Where the control socket and the audit log live [env: NERVE_NODE_STATE_DIR] [default: ~/.local/state/nerve, or /var/lib/nerve/state when installed as a service]
options.name: --state-dir <STATE_DIR>

options.more: Print JSON for programs instead of text: the read commands their data, the others the lines they print, an error {"error": ...}
options.name: --json

options.line: Which center, when more than one is paired
options.name: --center <CENTER>

args.line: Who owns the node: you (default), `root` (needs --accept-root-owner) or `none`
args.more: Run by root itself (Linux): `root` makes root the owner, so that user mode, and allowlist mode as the owner, run commands as root, with every right on the machine and over Nerve; needs --accept-root-owner. At a terminal install asks instead, and an owner root confirmed before stays. `none` leaves the node without an owner, root or another.
args.name: --owner <ACCOUNT>

args.line: Confirms --owner=root: nothing in Nerve holds those commands back
args.more: Confirms --owner=root: you accept that nothing in Nerve holds those commands back.
args.name: --accept-root-owner

verbs.line: Install the node as a service (Linux: with sudo; Windows: as administrator)
verbs.more: Install the node as a service that starts with the machine and runs under a user of its own, make the account nerve-run for its commands and take you as the owner (Linux with sudo from your own account, Windows as administrator).
verbs.name: install

args.line: Delete the config and state folders too (keys, pairings, audit)
args.more: Delete the config and state folders too: the keys, the pairings and the audit log.
args.name: --purge

verbs.line: Remove the service and the program; config and state stay
verbs.more: Stop and remove the service, nerve-run and its entries on your folders, the node's user and the program; the config and state folders stay.
verbs.name: uninstall

verbs.line: Pair a first center and give it a folder, step by step
verbs.more: Pair a first center and give it a folder, step by step: the link, the mode, a folder and its rights, the network.
verbs.name: setup

args.line: Take the new program from this file instead of downloading the latest release
args.name: --from <FILE>

verbs.line: Update to the latest release; config, keys and audit stay
verbs.more: Replace the installed program with the latest release and restart the service; config, keys and audit log stay.
verbs.name: update

shared_args.line: Read the passphrase from this file (`-`: from stdin) instead of asking
shared_args.more: Read the passphrase from the first line of this file instead of asking; `-` reads it from stdin.
shared_args.name: --passphrase-file <FILE>

args.line: The file to write. It is private to you (mode 0600)
args.name: <FILE>

args.line: Also take the keys that are in the system keyring into the file
args.more: Also take the keys that are in the system keyring into the file; without it they stay there and are left out.
args.name: --include-keyring

args.line: Replace the file when it exists
args.name: --overwrite

verbs.line: Save the config and keys to a passphrase-protected file
verbs.more: Write the config and the keys to a file that a passphrase protects, to keep or to move the node to another machine.
verbs.name: backup

args.line: The backup file
args.name: <FILE>

args.line: Replace a node here that is not the one the backup is of
args.name: --replace

args.line: Keep the keys in `file` or in the `keyring` here, whatever the backup says
args.more: Keep the keys in `file` or in the system `keyring` here, whatever the backup's config says.
args.name: --secret-storage <file|keyring>

args.line: Leave the proxy, with its secrets, out of the restored config
args.more: Leave the proxy out of the restored config, with its password and header values; set it again on this machine.
args.name: --without-proxy

verbs.line: Restore a backup (stop the node first)
verbs.more: Put the config and keys of a backup in place of this node's. The node must not run.
verbs.name: restore

cards.line: Start, stop or restart the installed service (`status` shows its state)
cards.name: service

verbs.line: Start the installed service; the owner needs no root or administrator for it
verbs.name: service start

verbs.line: Stop the service: the node ends its links and runs nothing
verbs.more: Stop it: the node ends its links and runs nothing until it starts again, at the latest with the machine.
verbs.name: service stop

verbs.line: Stop it and start it again, so the node takes every change in node.toml
verbs.name: service restart

sections.line: Install the node as a service, set it up, keep it current, and back it up.
sections.name: Set up

cards.line: Show the paired centers, pair another, and set what each may change
cards.more: Show the paired centers, pair this machine with another, and decide what each one may change.
cards.name: center

shared_args.line: The center's name; needed when more than one is paired
shared_args.name: <NAME>

verbs.line: Show the paired centers, pair another, and set what each may change
verbs.more: Show the paired centers, pair this machine with another, and decide what each one may change.
verbs.name: center

args.line: The pairing link; `-` reads it from stdin (never in the process list)
args.more: The pairing link; `-` reads it from the first line of stdin, where it never shows in the process list.
args.name: <LINK>

args.line: The name to use for the center here (the center's own name if left out)
args.name: --name <NAME>

args.line: Do not ask before pairing
args.name: --yes

verbs.line: Pair this machine with a center, using the pairing link it showed
verbs.name: center add

verbs.line: Forget a center and delete its key
verbs.name: center rm

verbs.line: Stop the link to a center until you resume it
verbs.name: center pause

verbs.line: Link to a paused center again
verbs.name: center resume

args.line: End the 7 days now: the center takes only the new key from then on
args.name: --end-grace

verbs.line: Give this machine a new key for a center (the node must run)
verbs.more: Give this machine a new key for a center; the center takes the old one for 7 more days. Needs the running node, linked to that center.
verbs.name: center rotate-key

args.line: `on` or `off`
args.name: <STATE>

verbs.line: Let a center change its own rights here (`on`), up to user mode and sudo
verbs.more: Let a center change its own rights on this machine, up to user mode and sudo (`on`), or take that right away (`off`).
verbs.name: center settings

args.line: `folder` (default; reads what all accounts may), `allowlist`, `user` (as you)
args.more: `allowlist` (only what an allow rule names, as nerve-run), `folder` (what each folder's rights allow, as nerve-run, the default; on the installed node a file call may also read what every account may read) or `user` (anything you could do yourself, as you, protected files aside). Without it, each center's mode is shown.
args.name: <MODE>

args.line: End the mode after this many hours (user: back to the mode before)
args.more: End the mode after this many hours: user goes back to the mode before it, folder to allowlist (without it they stay until you change them).
args.name: --for <HOURS>

args.line: With allowlist: run the allowed commands as you, outside the sandbox
args.more: With allowlist: run the allowed commands as you instead of as nerve-run, outside the folders' sandbox (installed node, Linux).
args.name: --as-owner

verbs.line: Choose how much a center may do: folder, allowlist or user mode (as you)
verbs.more: Show each center's mode, or choose how much a center may do: only what allow rules name, what each folder allows (as nerve-run, an account of its own), or all you can do (as you).
verbs.name: mode

cards.line: Show a center's folders, or choose them and their rights
cards.more: Show a center's folders, or choose the folders it may use and what it may do in each.
cards.name: folder

verbs.line: Show a center's folders, or choose them and their rights
verbs.more: Show a center's folders, or choose the folders it may use and what it may do in each.
verbs.name: folder

args.line: The rights, one word: `r`, `rw`, `rwx` and so on, or `none`
args.name: <RIGHTS>

verbs.line: Let a center use a folder (r, w, x); none closes one to file calls only
verbs.more: Let a center use a folder, or change what it may do in one it has: `r` reads, `w` writes and reads, `x` runs commands (`rw`, `rx`). `none` closes a folder inside one it may use to file calls; a command run in the folder around it still reaches it.
verbs.name: folder add

verbs.line: Take a folder away from a center
verbs.name: folder rm

verbs.line: Give nerve-run its access to every granted folder again (installed Linux node)
verbs.more: Give nerve-run its access to everything in the folders of every center again, also what was moved into them (the installed node on Linux): a pass over every granted folder.
verbs.name: folder sync

args.line: `off` or `on`; without it, each center's network is shown
args.name: <STATE>

verbs.line: Keep a center's commands off the network (`off`); in user mode nothing runs
verbs.more: Keep a center's commands off the network, or let them on it again: `off` lets them open no socket but a unix one, in every mode, and no sudo-list command runs; where they run as you (user mode, allowlist --as-owner) or the machine cannot hold them, none of them runs.
verbs.name: network

cards.line: Show a center's rules, or keep its lists of allowed and forbidden commands
cards.more: Show a center's rules, or keep its lists of commands that are allowed, forbidden or run with sudo.
cards.name: rule

args.line: The list to show: `allow`, `deny` or `sudo`; all three if left out
args.name: <LIST>

verbs.line: Show a center's rules, or keep its lists of allowed and forbidden commands
verbs.more: Show a center's rules, or keep its lists of commands that are allowed, forbidden or run with sudo.
verbs.name: rule

args.line: `allow` (in allowlist mode; a sudo command: with sudo) or `deny` (never runs)
args.more: The list: `allow` (may run in allowlist mode; a sudo command may run with sudo while sudo is on) or `deny` (a command line that matches never runs, in any mode).
args.name: <LIST>

args.line: The command line; a trailing ` *` covers what starts with the words before it
args.more: The command line; a trailing ` *` covers every command that starts with the words before it.
args.name: <COMMAND>

args.line: Make the rule from an audit entry's action, as the audit buttons do
args.more: Make the rule of an audit entry of this action instead, as the audit buttons do: `fs.read` takes a path (`/srv/data/*` covers the folder), an action without a target takes "" (`*` covers its capability).
args.name: --action <CAP.ACTION>

args.line: With --action: hold the rule to one argument, like room=office
args.more: With --action: hold the rule to one argument of the call, as the audit buttons do: `--arg room=office` makes `lamp.set:room=office`.
args.name: --arg <FIELD=VALUE>

args.line: With --action: take the target as it is, a `*` in it too (the exact buttons)
args.more: With --action: take the target as the audit entry has it, a `*` at its end too, so that `rm -rf *` stays that one command. The audit's Allow and Deny buttons make their rule so; without it a trailing `*` is the wildcard.
args.name: --exact

verbs.line: Allow or forbid a command; `sudo …` goes on the sudo list, ` *` is a wildcard
verbs.more: Put a command on a list; one that starts with `sudo` goes on the sudo list. A trailing ` *` covers every command that starts so (`'git status *'`).
verbs.name: rule add

args.line: The list, needed only when the entry is on two; then the entry
args.more: The list (`allow`, `deny` or `sudo`), needed only when the entry is on two; then the entry.
args.name: <ENTRY>

verbs.line: Take a rule off its list, as `rule` shows it
verbs.more: Take an entry off its list: the entry as `rule` shows it, or the command line that made it.
verbs.name: rule rm

args.line: The list: `allow`, `deny` or `sudo`
args.name: <LIST>

args.line: The entry as `rule` shows it
args.name: <ENTRY>

args.line: The new rule, as `rule` shows it, or a plain command line
args.more: What it becomes: an entry as `rule` shows them (`exec.run:git status`, `fs.read:~/notes/*`; on the sudo list a sudo command's pattern), or a plain command line, which becomes the rule `add` makes of it.
args.name: <NEW>

verbs.line: Change one rule in place, as one change
verbs.more: Change one entry of a list in place, as one change: the entry as `rule` shows it, and what it becomes.
verbs.name: rule edit

cards.line: Show whether sudo is on, or use sudo for the commands on the sudo list
cards.name: sudo

verbs.line: Show whether sudo is on, or use sudo for the commands on the sudo list
verbs.name: sudo

verbs.line: Turn sudo on; the password stays in memory only
verbs.more: Turn sudo on; asks for your sudo password (on Windows the password of the account commands run as) and keeps it in memory only, so a restart turns sudo off.
verbs.name: sudo on

verbs.line: Turn sudo off and forget the password
verbs.name: sudo off

sections.line: Every center has its own rights on this machine.
sections.name: What a center may do

verbs.line: Show how the node is: its service, each center, and what to do next
verbs.name: status

cards.line: Show what the node allowed and refused
cards.name: audit

args.line: Keep running and print new entries as they arrive
args.name: --follow

args.line: Show only the calls that were refused
args.name: --refused

args.line: Show only the newest N entries (with --follow, then the new ones)
args.name: --last <N>

verbs.line: Show what the node allowed and refused
verbs.name: audit

verbs.line: Start the audit log afresh (the old one becomes audit.jsonl.1)
verbs.more: Start the audit log afresh. The entries so far become its one older file (audit.jsonl.1, in place of the one before), and the new log begins with an entry of who cleared it.
verbs.name: audit clear

cards.line: Show the node's log: its starts and stops, its links, and what went wrong
cards.name: log

args.line: Keep running and print new lines as they arrive
args.name: --follow

args.line: Show only the newest N lines (with --follow, then the new ones)
args.name: --last <N>

args.line: Show only errors and warnings (with --last, the newest N of them)
args.name: --problems

verbs.line: Show the node's log: its starts and stops, its links, and what went wrong
verbs.name: log

verbs.line: Empty the node's log and its older file
verbs.more: Empty the node's log and its older file. The new log begins with a line of who cleared it.
verbs.name: log clear

verbs.line: Stop everything at once; nothing runs until `unlock`
verbs.name: panic

verbs.line: Let the node work again after `panic`
verbs.name: unlock

sections.line: See what the node did, and stop it.
sections.name: Watch and stop

cards.line: Turn capabilities on or off, and add your own
cards.more: Show every capability, turn capabilities and single actions on or off, and declare capabilities of your own in node.toml.
cards.name: cap

shared_args.line: What it does: read, write, execute, sense or actuate
shared_args.more: What it does: read, write, execute, sense or actuate. Sense and actuate need your `cap set NAME on` for a center.
shared_args.name: --effect <EFFECT>

shared_args.line: One line for the agent: what it does
shared_args.name: --summary <SUMMARY>

shared_args.line: JSON Schema of its arguments, `none`, or `-` for stdin
shared_args.more: The JSON Schema of its arguments, an object; `none` takes no arguments; `-` reads it from stdin. A property marked "x-nerve-path": "read" or "write" is a path the node holds to the folders.
shared_args.name: --params <JSON>

shared_args.line: What it returns: `text` (the default), or a JSON Schema; `-` for stdin
shared_args.more: What it returns: `text`, what the command prints (the default), or a JSON Schema the printed JSON must fit; `-` reads it from stdin.
shared_args.name: --result <text|JSON>

shared_args.line: How long it may run, in seconds, or `default`
shared_args.more: How long it may run, in seconds, up to limits.max_timeout_secs; `default` for the node's default.
shared_args.name: --timeout <SECS>

shared_args.line: Where it runs: any (the default), linux or windows
shared_args.more: Where it runs: any (the default), linux or windows. A node offers only those of its platform.
shared_args.name: --platform <PLATFORM>

args.line: Only this center's settings
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.line: Turn capabilities on or off, and add your own
verbs.more: Show every capability, turn capabilities and single actions on or off, and declare capabilities of your own in node.toml.
verbs.name: cap

args.line: The capability (`fs`) or action (`exec.run`)
args.name: <CAP>

args.line: `on`, `off` or `hidden`
args.name: <SETTING>

verbs.line: Set a capability (`fs`) or one action (`exec.run`) to on, off or hidden
verbs.name: cap set

args.line: `cap.action`, like sensors.read
args.name: <NAME>

args.line: The program and its arguments, after `--`
args.name: <COMMAND>

verbs.line: Declare a capability that runs a fixed command (the words after `--`)
verbs.more: Declare a capability of your own, NAME (`cap.action`, like sensors.read), that runs a fixed command: the words after `--`, the program first. A word written `{field}` is the call's argument `field`, as one whole argument; no shell reads it. It runs as nerve-run on the installed Linux node, held to the folders; a node run by hand offers none.
verbs.name: cap add

args.line: The program and its arguments, after `--`
args.name: <COMMAND>

verbs.line: Change a capability you declared
verbs.more: Change a capability you declared: what you give replaces what it has, and a command after `--` its command.
verbs.name: cap edit

args.line: The center that added it, for a capability a center added
args.name: --center <CENTER>

verbs.line: Remove a capability you declared (from every center at once)
verbs.more: Remove a capability you declared; it leaves every center at once. With --center, remove one that center added itself (settings on); `cap set NAME off --center` turns it off instead.
verbs.name: cap rm

cards.line: Show the programs that may add capabilities (providers), allow one, or remove it
cards.name: provider

verbs.line: Show the programs that may add capabilities (providers), allow one, or remove it
verbs.name: provider

args.line: The provider's name, which its capabilities carry: 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and `-`
args.name: <NAME>

args.line: The full path of the program's executable
args.name: <EXE>

verbs.line: Allow the program EXE to add capabilities as provider NAME
verbs.more: Let the program EXE attach as the provider NAME; it replaces the program allowed under that name. The node checks that the program that attaches runs this very file.
verbs.name: provider add

args.line: The provider's name
args.name: <NAME>

verbs.line: Remove the program allowed as NAME; its capabilities leave at once
verbs.name: provider rm

cards.line: Show or choose the proxy the node uses to reach centers
cards.name: proxy

verbs.line: Show or choose the proxy the node uses to reach centers
verbs.name: proxy

args.line: http://[user[:password]@]host:port, https://…, a nerve://relay link; - for stdin
args.more: The proxy, http://host:port, or http://user:password@host:port when it wants a login (http://user@host:port asks for the password, or reads it from the next line of stdin); https://... for another proxy reached over TLS; or the nerve://relay link a relay showed, which holds its address, pin and this node's token. `-` reads it from the first line of stdin, where it never shows in the process list.
args.name: <URL>

args.line: The pin of an https:// proxy's certificate
args.more: The pin of an https:// proxy's certificate (a relay's: `nerve-node relay` there shows it); without it the system's roots check it.
args.name: --pin <PIN>

args.line: A header for the proxy, `Name: value`, kept in the keyring; `-` for stdin
args.more: A header for the proxy, `Name: value`; can be given more than once. The value goes into the system keyring. `-` reads headers from stdin, one a line, after the password.
args.name: --header <NAME: VALUE>

verbs.line: Reach centers through an HTTP proxy or a relay
verbs.more: Reach centers through an HTTP proxy. Header values and a password are kept in the system keyring, never in node.toml; the installed node on Windows takes neither.
verbs.name: proxy set

verbs.line: Reach centers directly again, without a proxy
verbs.more: Reach centers directly again, and delete the proxy's values from the system keyring.
verbs.name: proxy off

cards.line: Let other nodes reach your centers through this node
cards.more: Let nodes that cannot reach a center themselves reach this node's centers through it.
cards.name: relay

verbs.line: Let other nodes reach your centers through this node
verbs.more: Let nodes that cannot reach a center themselves reach this node's centers through it.
verbs.name: relay

args.line: The address and port to listen on, like 0.0.0.0:7490 or [::]:7490
args.name: <ADDRESS>

args.line: Tunnels at once, over every relayed node (16 unless set)
args.name: --max-links <N>

args.line: Tunnels at once of one relayed node (4 unless set)
args.name: --max-links-per-node <N>

args.line: Tunnels one relayed node may open per minute (30)
args.more: Tunnels one relayed node may open a minute, every node alike (30 unless set; for a relay behind this one, use `relay set <name>`).
args.name: --max-opens-per-minute <N>

verbs.line: Turn the relay on at ADDRESS, like 0.0.0.0:7490
verbs.more: Turn the relay on: listen for other nodes at ADDRESS, like 0.0.0.0:7490. A node reaches only this node's own https centers through it.
verbs.name: relay on

verbs.line: Turn the relay off; its nodes and their tokens stay
verbs.more: Turn the relay off: stop listening and end every tunnel. The nodes and their tokens stay.
verbs.name: relay off

args.line: The relayed node's name here: 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -
args.more: The relayed node's name here, 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
args.name: <NAME>

args.line: A center it may reach (more than once); without it, every one
args.more: A center of this node the relayed node may reach; can be given more than once. Without it, every one.
args.name: --to <CENTER>

args.line: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST[:PORT], for its link
args.more: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST or HOST:PORT, for its link (without it: the address the relay listens on, else this machine's host name).
args.name: --address <HOST[:PORT]>

verbs.line: Let a node use the relay (shows its link once)
verbs.more: Let a node use the relay: makes its token and shows it once, in a link the other node pastes. Without --to its tunnels may go to every https center of this node.
verbs.name: relay add

args.line: A center it may reach (more than once); `*` for every one
args.more: A center of this node the relayed node may reach; can be given more than once; `*` for every one.
args.name: --to <CENTER>

args.line: Its tunnels at once; `default` for the relay's --max-links-per-node
args.name: --max-links <N>

args.line: The tunnels it may open a minute; `default` for the relay's
args.name: --max-opens-per-minute <N>

verbs.line: Change the centers or the limits of one relayed node
verbs.more: Change what a relayed node may: the centers it may reach (its tunnels to others end), and limits of its own in place of the relay's, for a relay behind this one, which carries many nodes. What is not given stays.
verbs.name: relay set

args.line: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST[:PORT], for its link
args.more: Where the other node reaches this machine, HOST or HOST:PORT, for its link (as for `relay add`).
args.name: --address <HOST[:PORT]>

verbs.line: Give a relayed node a new token (shows its link once)
verbs.more: Give a relayed node a new token and end the tunnels of the old one; its centers and limits stay. Shows the token once, in a link the other node pastes.
verbs.name: relay token

verbs.line: Take a node's token away and end its tunnels
verbs.name: relay rm

cards.line: Turn the node's web UI on or off, and manage its tokens
cards.more: Turn the node's web UI on or off, and make the tokens that log in to it (the installed node on Linux; off unless turned on).
cards.name: ui

verbs.line: Turn the node's web UI on or off, and manage its tokens
verbs.more: Turn the node's web UI on or off, and make the tokens that log in to it (the installed node on Linux; off unless turned on).
verbs.name: ui

args.line: Address and port (127.0.0.1:7470); any other address opens it to the network
args.more: The address and port to listen on (127.0.0.1:7470 unless set). Any address but loopback, like 0.0.0.0:7470, makes the UI reachable from the network.
args.name: --listen <ADDRESS>

args.line: A host name for the certificate, besides this machine's own (more than once)
args.more: A host name the certificate names besides this machine's own and the address; can be given more than once.
args.name: --host <HOST>

args.line: Make a new certificate: every session ends, and the browser asks about it again
args.name: --new-cert

verbs.line: Turn the web UI on (shows a first token once)
verbs.more: Turn the web UI on. With no token yet, makes one named `first` and shows it once. Beyond loopback it is served over TLS with a certificate of its own, made the first time; compare its fingerprint with the one the browser shows.
verbs.name: ui on

verbs.line: Turn the web UI off: it stops listening and every session ends. Its tokens stay
verbs.name: ui off

cards.line: List the tokens that log in to the web UI by label, make one, or revoke one
cards.name: ui token

verbs.line: List the tokens that log in to the web UI by label, make one, or revoke one
verbs.name: ui token

args.line: Its label, 1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -
args.name: <LABEL>

verbs.line: Make a token and show it once
verbs.name: ui token add

args.line: The token's label
args.name: <LABEL>

verbs.line: Revoke a token; the sessions it opened end at once
verbs.name: ui token rm

cards.line: Read or change any setting in node.toml by its name
cards.name: config

shared_args.line: The dotted key of the setting, like `center.<name>.policy.mode`
shared_args.name: <KEY>

shared_args.line: The dotted key of a list, like `center.<name>.policy.allow`
shared_args.name: <KEY>

verbs.line: Print one setting
verbs.name: config get

args.line: The new value
args.name: <VALUE>

verbs.line: Change one setting
verbs.name: config set

verbs.line: Remove one setting (its default applies again)
